# Configuration file

Every key `ITdSecScan.config` accepts, read out of the list the scanner itself
uses to load the file. A key not listed here is ignored.

The file sits beside the executable (`-config` points elsewhere). One key per
line as `KEY=value`; blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored, and a
value may be wrapped in single or double quotes. With profiles, each
`ITdSecScan.<name>.config` holds the same keys for its own environment, and
every key is reset between profiles, so one customer's value never reaches the
next.

A minimal Windows configuration for a domain and its tenant:

```
CUSTOMER_NAME=Contoso GmbH
AD_LDAP_URL=ldap://dc01.contoso.com:389
AD_BASE_DN=DC=contoso,DC=com
AD_AUTH_MODE=windows_current_user
AZURE_TENANT_ID=<tenant id>
AZURE_CLIENT_ID=<application id>
AZURE_AUTH_MODE=cert_store
AZURE_CERT_THUMBPRINT=<thumbprint>
```

## Report

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `CUSTOMER_NAME` | — | Customer name in the heading of every report. Without it the heading names the scanned domain. `-customer` overrides it for one run. |

## Active Directory

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `AD_LDAP_URL` | — | LDAP server, `ldap://dc01.contoso.com:389` or `ldaps://dc01.contoso.com:636`. Required for the AD checks. |
| `AD_BASE_DN` | — | Search base, normally the domain root: `DC=contoso,DC=com`. Required for the AD checks. |
| `AD_AUTH_MODE` | `simple_bind` | `windows_current_user` (Windows: Kerberos as the logged-on user, no password), `simple_bind` (DN and password), or `keychain` (macOS: DN from the config, password from the Keychain). |
| `AD_BIND_DN` | — | Account to bind as, for `simple_bind` and `keychain`. |
| `AD_BIND_PASSWORD` | — | Its password, for `simple_bind`. Prefer `keychain` on macOS and `windows_current_user` on Windows, so no password sits in the file. |
| `AD_KEYCHAIN_SERVICE` | `mcp-ad-ldap` | Keychain service name the password is stored under, for `keychain`. |
| `AD_KEYCHAIN_ACCOUNT` | value of `AD_BIND_DN` | Keychain account name, for `keychain`. |
| `AD_KRB_SERVICE_PRINCIPAL` | `ldap/<host of AD_LDAP_URL>` | Kerberos service principal for `windows_current_user`. Only needed when the URL names a host the DC's SPN does not. |
| `AD_LDAP_STARTTLS` | `false` | `true` upgrades an `ldap://` connection with StartTLS, for DCs that require LDAP signing. |
| `AD_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY` | `false` | `true` accepts a DC certificate that does not validate. For a lab only: it makes the connection open to interception. |
| `AD_PAGE_SIZE` | `500` | LDAP paged-search size. |
| `AD_SYSVOL_PATH` | `/Volumes/<share>` | macOS/Linux: where SYSVOL is mounted, for the Group Policy checks. Windows reads the UNC path directly. |

## Entra ID

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `AZURE_TENANT_ID` | — | Tenant ID. With `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` it enables the Entra checks; without both they are skipped. |
| `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` | — | Application (client) ID of the scanning app registration. |
| `AZURE_AUTH_MODE` | from the keys set | `cert_store` (Windows certificate store, recommended), `certificate` (PFX/PEM file) or `secret` (client secret). Without it: `cert_store` if a thumbprint is set, `certificate` if a file is, else `secret`. |
| `AZURE_CERT_THUMBPRINT` | — | Certificate thumbprint, for `cert_store`. |
| `AZURE_CERT_STORE_NAME` | `MY` | Certificate store, for `cert_store`. |
| `AZURE_CERT_PATH` | — | Path to the PFX or PEM file, for `certificate`. |
| `AZURE_CERT_PASSWORD` | — | PFX password, for `certificate`. On macOS use the Keychain keys below instead. |
| `AZURE_CERT_KEYCHAIN_SERVICE` | `mcp-ad-ldap` | macOS: Keychain service holding the PFX password. |
| `AZURE_CERT_KEYCHAIN_ACCOUNT` | — | macOS: Keychain account holding the PFX password. Setting it turns the Keychain lookup on. |
| `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` | — | Client secret, for `secret`. Expires and has to be rotated; a certificate does not need a secret in the file. |

## Storage

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `BASELINE_DIR` | `./baselines` | Where baselines, accepted risks and to-dos are stored. `-output` overrides it for one run. |
